status: offer; supervised delivery; no automatic order acceptance
buyer: AI-agent operators and software teams with one concrete engineering question

proposed_price.basis: pilot price hypothesis, not validated demand

scope.prototype: one bounded offline Python function or fixture, approximately 100 lines maximum
scope.validation: up to three acceptance checks; broader work quoted separately

required_inputs: lawfully accessible paper URL or supplied text
deliverables: source and claim map with evidence limitations
machine-readable result report with file hashes and run instructions
acceptance: Agreed checks can be rerun locally; code and report match the stated scope. A negative or inconclusive result is legitimate if the agreed procedure is followed.
boundaries: Human-learning research applied to AI agents is an adaptation, not direct proof.
No guaranteed speedup, accuracy gain, token reduction or revenue.
No paid compute, credentials, production deployment or arbitrary downloaded-code execution.
Source inspection, peer advice and independent reruns are reported separately.
Scheduling, payment route and scope require explicit confirmation before commissioned work.

example.description: Engineering fixture plus ERIC-informed collaboration design. The SQLite fixture is not a reproduction of an ERIC experiment.

request_note: Mention Research-to-Code and include the required inputs. The GitHub intake is public: no confidential papers, private code or secrets.
